summary: Produces developer INTEGRATION RECIPES for the Learnosity Author API — a precise, host-language-neutral procedure (goal, preconditions, steps, gotchas, verification steps) for embedding and configuring an integrated item/activity authoring experience (the Learnosity item/activity editor and browser) in a host app. The client describes the integration design; L0177 flags holes in the design and returns how to implement it. It emits a recipe to follow, NOT Learnosity item content and NOT runnable code. Knowledge combines documentation with direct API observations. Modeled scope and empirical coverage are distinct; the caller implements and verifies the recipe in their environment.
boundary_rule: The dividing line across the Learnosity dialects is "I want the data" vs "I want a UX of the data" — two views of the same underlying thing. L0177 is a UX plane: the authoring experience over an Item bank. L0178 is the DATA plane for the whole family and covers all of the Data API. L0176 sits off the axis, composing item CONTENT — the payload L0178 transports. L0176 composes, L0178 moves, L0177 renders for humans. Route on that axis, not on which vendor API a call belongs to.
in_scope: How to embed the Learnosity Author API item editor (item_edit) in a host/LMS app
How to embed the item browser/list (item_list), the activity editor (activity_edit), or the activity list (activity_list) — all four Author API views have their configuration modeled

How to configure what an embedded LIST or BROWSER displays — which columns/fields appear (titles, references, status), page size, and which items or activities are shown (filter by status, tags, creator, item bank). A request phrased as "list/show activities with titles and status, 15 per page" or "only show items tagged Subject: Math" is CONFIGURING AN EMBEDDED BROWSER VIEW, not querying data: the answer is item_list/activity_list view options, and it belongs here
How to configure the authoring experience: allowed widget/question types, editor permissions (edit/delete widgets, edit/show tags), shared passages, dynamic content, container sizing, which item bank
How to sign the Author API init request with the official Learnosity server-side SDK, and the domain-match / timestamp rules
How to wire the client-side readyListener / errorListener callbacks
The verification steps that tell the developer their authoring integration works (what 'done' looks like)
out_of_scope: Authoring the assessment item CONTENT itself (stems, options, answer keys, passages) — that is L0176; this dialect describes how to INTEGRATE the authoring experience, it does not write items

Retrieving, paging through, or reporting ON the data itself — returning a list of activities to a caller, exporting item records, counting or aggregating them. The distinction from the in-scope entry above is WHO consumes the result: configuring an embedded browser tells Learnosity's UI what to render for an author, while a data query returns rows to your code. Wording overlaps heavily ("list", "show", "filter", "per page") and MUST NOT be read as a data operation when the subject is an embedded authoring view

Creating/managing items programmatically via the Data API (item bank CRUD) — that is L0178, the data plane. L0177 is the UX plane over the same Item bank: it describes how a PERSON edits items in a browser, not how a PROGRAM reads or writes them server-to-server. The item CONTENT itself is L0176's surface. If the request is for extraction, bulk load, or any programmatic bank access, send it to L0178 rather than answering here.

Delivering/administering assessments to learners (Items API) and rendering reports for a human (Reports API) — each is its own UX-plane sibling dialect, and neither is built. Say no dialect covers it rather than stretching this one. Note the raw session and score DATA behind those experiences is L0178's, not a gap: only the rendered experience is unbuilt.

Defining custom assessment player templates (activity_edit.player_templates) — past a name and reference these are Assess API configuration (labelBundle, regions, navigation) passed through the Author API, so describing them means describing Assess API, which this dialect does not cover. Pick a template by reference with default-player-template / enabled-player-templates instead
Integrations for any platform other than Learnosity
Emitting runnable host-language code — the recipe is a language-neutral procedure the caller implements in their own stack
